scopeSummary: Candidate responsibilities discovered by starting in resources/ launch scripts and test/ CLI and editor-restart scenarios, then following remote command dispatch and working-copy backup implementation. This is a bounded source inspection of the pinned snapshot, not exhaustive coverage or runtime verification.

omissions: Both selected regions were inspected: resources/ through three Linux entry scripts, and test/ through one complete CLI sanity test plus the first 160 lines of editor data-loss smoke scenarios. Other files in both regions remain unread.
Only selected windows of the remote CLI and common/native backup trackers were inspected; browser backup tracker and CLI pipe-server implementation were read completely.
The CLI sanity test only checks packaged CLI commit output and is not evidence of remote editor commands working.

No macOS or Windows launcher implementation, complete editor-tab restoration implementation, backup storage backend, working-copy-specific content restoration, or main-thread remote command handler was inspected.

Source retrieval exhausted practically all serialized receipt bytes before the window limit: 16 source windows and 4 successful search receipts total 71931 serialized bytes. Searches were navigation only.

crossPartitionLeads: resources/server/bin/remote-cli/code-linux.sh led to src/vs/server/node/server.cli.ts (partition B); its PipeCommand import led to src/vs/workbench/api/node/extHostCLIServer.ts (partition A).
test/smoke/src/areas/workbench/data-loss.test.ts (partition A) supplied restart scenarios; scoped workingCopy navigation led to common, desktop, and browser backup trackers (partition C).

The CLI pipe server forwards to _remoteCLI.windowOpen, _remoteCLI.openExternal, _remoteCLI.manageExtensions and _remoteCLI.getSystemStatus. Scoped listing located mainThreadCLICommands.ts, but its contents could not be retrieved within the remaining byte budget. These downstream behaviors remain leads, not inspected support.

nodes.name: Open editor resources from a remote terminal
nodes.summary: Translate remote terminal file, folder and standard-input requests into workbench opening commands, carrying window, comparison, line-location and wait options.
nodes.actor: Developer invoking the editor command from a remote integrated terminal or a configured WSL terminal
inputs: Positional paths, file and folder URIs, or '-' for non-TTY standard input
Remote CLI environment and supported window, diff, merge, goto and wait arguments
outcomes: Paths and standard-input temporary files become file/folder URI opening requests
Pipe requests are converted to _remoteCLI.windowOpen arguments
A wait request keeps the CLI polling until its marker file disappears
conditions: The CLI returns without action if neither VSCODE_IPC_HOOK_CLI nor VSCODE_CLIENT_COMMAND is set
The pipe wait path requires at least one file URI
Supported options differ between direct client-command and pipe routes
exclusions: Remote agent command execution is explicitly rejected
Actual window creation, diff/merge editing, and wait-marker deletion were not traced
Packaged CLI version checks do not establish this behavior
implementations: Linux remote-cli shell entry invokes server-cli.js with product information and arguments
server.cli.ts maps input paths, reads standard input, invokes a configured client command or posts an open request to the CLI pipe
extHostCLIServer.ts classifies workspace files and dispatches _remoteCLI.windowOpen
uncertainty: Static implementation supports the request path; downstream workbench opening and end-to-end operation were not independently checked
The client-command WSL branch was inspected but its invoked desktop CLI was not

claims.text: The remote CLI requires a pipe or client command environment, filters supported arguments and rejects the agent command.
For non-TTY input with '-', the CLI prepares a temporary file for opening, skips recent-history addition, and can remain alive while input streams.
The pipe route forwards file/folder URIs, comparison, window and line options; the server constructs window-open arguments, while --wait polls its marker file.
The complete remote terminal interaction opens the intended workbench resources and releases wait when editing ends.

nodes.name: Request external URL opening from a remote terminal
nodes.summary: Route browser-helper and remote CLI URL requests through the connected workbench, excluding remote file URLs at the receiving CLI server.
nodes.actor: Developer or remote process launching a URL through the provided browser helper
inputs: Locations supplied to the browser helper or --openExternal
outcomes: Valid locations become an openExternal URI request
Invalid URLs are reported and remote file URIs are skipped
conditions: The server CLI selects this path when the CLI pipe is present and openExternal is set
exclusions: Local opening of remote file:// resources
Browser choice, URL security decisions and final external application behavior
implementations: server.cli.ts openInBrowser normalizes locations and sends an openExternal message
extHostCLIServer.ts skips file-scheme URIs and dispatches the remaining URI strings
uncertainty: The downstream _remoteCLI.openExternal implementation and actual browser launch were not inspected or executed

claims.text: The Linux browser helper selects the remote CLI's --openExternal route, which creates a normalized URI request on the CLI pipe.
The receiving CLI server skips file-scheme URIs and forwards other URI strings to _remoteCLI.openExternal.
The request ultimately opens the URL in an external application on the connected workbench side.

nodes.name: Request extension management from a remote terminal
nodes.summary: Accept extension listing, installation and removal arguments in a remote terminal and route their parameters to the extension-management command path.
nodes.actor: Developer managing extensions through the remote editor CLI
inputs: Extension IDs or VSIX references for install or uninstall
Listing options for versions/category and a force flag
outcomes: The CLI sends an extensionManagement request over its pipe
The CLI server converts VSIX references into URIs and dispatches _remoteCLI.manageExtensions
Command results are printed and request errors are reported
conditions: CLI environment and option support gates apply
The direct client-command branch invokes server-main separately for extension-management requests
exclusions: Proving installation, update or uninstall completion
Marketplace resolution, download, compatibility checks and extension activation
Pipe-based extension update semantics are not established: the observed update flag enters the branch but is not a field in its outgoing management payload
implementations: extHostCLIServer.ts manageExtensions dispatch with VSIX conversion
uncertainty: The downstream management handler was located but not read
The installed-extension target and locality are not established by the inspected dispatch layer

claims.text: The pipe request carries list, install, uninstall and force fields; listing includes category and showVersions options.
The receiving server converts .vsix references to URIs and forwards arguments to _remoteCLI.manageExtensions.
The complete request performs the intended extension change or listing.

nodes.name: Back up and reopen unsaved editor work
nodes.summary: Track modified working-copy content for backup and associate retained backups with editors after startup so unsaved work can be recovered.
nodes.actor: Editor user with modified files, untitled content or another registered working-copy type
inputs: Working-copy dirty/content changes and content versions
Backup content and metadata provided by working copies
Stored backup identifiers and compatible editor handlers
outcomes: Modified content schedules a cancellable backup with version and metadata
Clean working copies discard their backups
Handled retained backups acquire editors, opened inactive and pinned while preserving focus, then unresolved non-visible editors are resolved
conditions: New content reschedules pending backup work and suspended tracking does not schedule changes
Backup delay follows working-copy overrides or untitled/auto-save policy
Backup enumeration waits for lifecycle Restored; restoration requires a handler that accepts the identifier
exclusions: Proof of persistent-storage durability or crash-loss bounds
Complete restoration of ordinary unmodified editor tabs
implementations: common/workingCopyBackupTracker.ts change tracking, backup scheduling/discard and editor restoration
Native shutdown tracker can reuse a matching-version backup or obtain and store a fresh one
data-loss.test.ts defines restart checks for dirty saved-file and untitled content
uncertainty: Backup storage and concrete working-copy resolve implementations were not read
Smoke-test expectations were inspected without running tests; they do not establish passing behavior at this snapshot

claims.text: Dirty and modified-content changes schedule cancellable versioned backups; clean working copies discard backups.
After lifecycle restoration, retained backup identifiers are matched to editor handlers; missing editors are opened without taking focus and non-visible associated editors are resolved.
Defined restart smoke scenarios expect both dirty file content and untitled content to survive, including immediate restart and a delayed restart.
Unsaved content is successfully recovered end to end after restart.

nodes.name: Resolve unsaved changes before leaving the editor
nodes.summary: Decide whether shutdown can proceed by auto-saving eligible content, applying hot-exit backup policy, or asking the user to save, discard or cancel; browser shutdown uses synchronous backup checks.
nodes.actor: User closing, quitting, reloading or changing the workspace with modified editors
inputs: Shutdown reason, platform/window context and hot-exit/auto-save settings
outcomes: Native shutdown first auto-saves eligible non-untitled copies
Qualifying modified copies are backed up and successful complete backup permits shutdown
Remaining changes trigger save/discard/cancel decisions, with failed or canceled saves vetoing shutdown
Browser shutdown is vetoed when hot exit is disabled or a matching content-version backup is absent
conditions: Hot-exit decisions differ for quit, reload, window close and workspace load
Window-close decisions depend on workspace state, settings, platform and window count
Scratchpads have specific backup handling during workspace/window changes
Extension-development mode has exceptional backup/error behavior
exclusions: Guaranteeing prevention of all data loss
Equivalent desktop and browser shutdown behavior
implementations: electron-browser/workingCopyBackupTracker.ts shutdown auto-save, backup policy, confirmation and save/revert orchestration
uncertainty: Native error-dialog choices were only partly inspected
No lifecycle integration or user interaction was executed
Backing-store failures and forced shutdown can limit protection

claims.text: Native shutdown attempts auto-save for eligible non-untitled modified copies, then uses configured hot-exit backup or confirmation for remaining changes.
The backup policy distinguishes quit/reload from close/load and conditions close/load behavior on workspace, platform, window count, settings and scratchpad status.
The save/discard/cancel path permits completed saving or reverting, but vetoes on canceled or insufficient saves and on user cancellation.
The browser final-shutdown path vetoes modified content when hot exit is disabled or any working copy lacks a backup matching its content version.

edges.reason: The hot-exit branch of shutdown protection consults matching-version backups or creates them; browser shutdown likewise permits modified copies only when matching backups exist. Other shutdown branches can save or discard instead.

limitations: All capability boundaries and relationships are candidate interpretations from static source at commit 33341eb227ab213b011868c9bc5c5f735aaaf875; no target code, tests, network or paid APIs were executed.
Inspected shell resources establish entry routing; no separate product capability was inferred merely from packaging or test tooling.

Remote CLI responsibilities share dispatch infrastructure, but their resource-opening, external-URL and extension-management requests have distinct inputs and downstream commands; no unsupported encompassing hierarchy was imposed.

A search for _remoteCLI.openExternal under src/vs/workbench was rejected on source blob src/vs/workbench/api/browser/mainThreadLanguageModels.ts and yielded no usable evidence. Subsequent scoped searches under contrib/remote and mainThreadCommands.ts returned no matches.

Reads of mainThreadCLICommands.ts at 1/160 and 20/50 were rejected because the evidence-byte budget would be exceeded; a 161/60 read was rejected because its start was beyond the file. The handler was never inspected and no claims cite it.
No proposal was used as independent verification, and no prior maps, baseline labels, other proposals, owner feedback, vault history or historical repository evidence were accessed.
